issues.failure_explanation: Both displayed transforms are unnormalized, so F^{-1}F = |I_m| Id. With the stated conventions the spreading transform is â_k = |I_m| Σ_r c_{k+mr}ρ̂(k+mr) ≈ (|I_m|/V)φ̂(k)ρ̂(k), not ρ̂(k)φ̂(k); after the deconvolution 1/φ̂(k)^2 and the unnormalized inverse transform the pipeline of Algorithm alg:SE_Fourier (and of eq:matform) returns (|I_m|^2/V^2)φ^far = h^{-6}φ^far instead of φ^far. No consistent choice of DFT normalization makes all displayed formulas correct: relative to a 1/|I_m|-normalized inverse transform the diagonal factor must be h^3(M̂/φ̂^2), not V^{-1}(M̂/φ̂^2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix the transform normalization consistently, e.g. use b̂_k = h^3 (M̂(k)/φ̂(k)^2) â_k together with a 1/|I_m|-normalized inverse FFT, and state eq:alias with the matching factor.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:SE_Fourier and the matrix form eq:matform return a constant multiple of the far-field potential; the claim â_k ≈ ρ̂(k)φ̂(k) and the aliasing identity eq:alias are mis-normalized by |I_m| (equivalently the inverse transform is missing 1/|I_m|). The error estimates, being stated in Fourier-series coefficients, are unaffected.
issues.title: Fast Fourier-space summation is mis-scaled by FFT normalization
issues.why_classification: A short, local change of normalization constants restores the algorithm's output scale and every guarantee; no lemma, construction or rate is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is unimportant in practice, since this region is never used.
The Fourier-transformed mollifier is evaluated at all available wavenumbers (also outside the bandlimit)

issues.failure_explanation: The closed form for the mollifier transform holds for radial frequencies |ω| ≤ c_s/r_c = ω_max = πm/L, i.e. for grid modes with |k| ≤ m/2. The algorithms sum over the whole cube I_m, whose corner modes have |k| up to (√3/2)m and hence |ω| up to √3 ω_max > c_s/r_c; roughly half of the volume of I_m lies outside the radial band. For those modes the closed form is invalid and the defining integral (or ψ̂) must be used, so the claim that the out-of-band region 'is never used' is false.

failure_location.quote: \eqref{eq:gammahatintegral} is never used in practice, since only Fourier modes within the band

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Evaluate γ̂_{r_c}^{c_s} at the corner modes from its defining integral (or via ψ̂_0^{c_s}) and delete the claim; alternatively truncate the Fourier sum to |k| ≤ m/2 and redo the truncation analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The practical simplification advertised in Section 4.2 and in the caption of Table tab:mollifiers is wrong: the out-of-band transform is needed for a large fraction of the modes, as the paper's own reference computation admits. The same out-of-band values enter the mollifier factor of the aliasing bound, where the closed form is nevertheless used (see ISSUE-004).
issues.title: False claim that all required Fourier modes lie inside the PSWF band
issues.why_classification: Computing the mollifier transform at the out-of-band modes by quadrature is routine and preserves the method, the error rates and the parameter rules; only the false claim is withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: until slowly decaying $\mathrm{sinc}$-type oscillations in the PSWF spectrum dominate the total error
which provides an error estimate for the far-field direct sum for a general mollifier $\gamma_{\sigma}$.

issues.failure_explanation: |M̂(ω)|^2 = 16π^2|γ̂_σ(ω)|^2/ω^4 is not nonincreasing in |ω| for the mollifiers considered. For the compactly supported PSWF mollifier the spectrum is a decaying sinc-type oscillation (|γ̂| ≈ 2ψ(1)|sin(r_cω)|/(λψ(0) r_c ω) outside the band, as the paper itself notes), so |M̂|^2 has infinitely many local maxima; for a general even nonnegative mollifier (e.g. a rescaled indicator) γ̂ is a sinc and is again non-monotone. The lattice-to-continuum estimate of Lemma lem:cubecover requires a nonincreasing integrand, so the passage from the lattice sum to the radial integral is not justified. (The same display also sums over the complement of the Euclidean ball |k| > K_max although the truncation retains the cube I_m.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the monotone covering step by a comparison valid for oscillatory radial profiles (e.g. apply the covering bound to a nonincreasing radial envelope of |M̂|^2, or a bounded-variation version of the lattice comparison) and re-collect constants.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lemma:dirsumerr_L2's estimate is unproved, and with it Proposition prop:PSWF_split_errors, the split-error model eq:PSWF_model and the c_s selection rule of Algorithm alg:parameter.
issues.title: Truncation bound relies on false monotonicity of the mollified spectrum
issues.why_classification: A replacement lattice-comparison argument for non-monotone (sinc-oscillating) spectra is required, which is more than a local edit, but the statement's form, the exponential rates and all parameter guarantees survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:PSWFrelation gives ψ̂_0^c(ω) = λ_0 ψ_0^c(ω/c) only for |ω| ≤ c. The proof of Proposition prop:interpol_est substitutes this identity into the numerator of the aliasing ratio at the shifted modes k+mr, whose arguments 2(k_i+mr_i)/m lie in [1,3] (as the paper itself computes), i.e. at frequencies up to 3c_w where the tables state that no closed form exists. The displayed ratio is therefore not the ratio of Fourier-series coefficients of the window, and eq:interpol_est contains values of ψ_0^{c_w} outside [-1,1], where the paper never defines it (and where a literal ODE/Legendre extension is O(1), not O(e^{-c_w}), making the bound false). The same substitution is used for the mollifier factor ψ_0^{c_s}(2|k|/m) at corner modes with 2|k|/m up to √3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the aliasing estimate using the true transforms ψ̂_0^{c_w}, ψ̂_0^{c_s} outside the band (bounded through the edge values ψ_0(1) and their 1/|ω| decay) and re-sum over the cube; refit the constant A_w if needed.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:interpol_est's bound is unsupported and partly ill-defined; the closed-form aliasing model eq:window_err_model, the balancing rule eq:cwW and the c_w step of Algorithm alg:parameter inherit the defect, so the advertised accuracy control is not established.
issues.title: Aliasing bound applies the in-band PSWF transform identity outside its range
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new bound on the out-of-band PSWF transform and a contained re-derivation of the aliasing sum (with possible refitting of constants), but the e^{-c_w} rate, the model's structure and the parameter scheme survive, so no major loss occurs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We then solve \eqref{eq:cwcs_model_dimless} for $c_w$ using the Lambert $W$ function and obtain

issues.failure_explanation: The argument -2 B_w^2 e^{-2c_s}/c_s lies in (-1/e,0), where the real Lambert W function has two branches, and the balancing equation √c_w e^{-c_w} = const genuinely has two positive solutions (c ↦ √c e^{-c} is unimodal with maximum at c = 1/2). The formula c_w = -W(...)/2 is therefore ambiguous: the principal branch returns c_w ≈ 0 (about 1.3e-10 for the paper's test values r_c = 0.1, L = 1, c_s = 10), giving a degenerate window with P = 0 or 1 and destroying the accuracy, while the W_{-1} branch gives the intended c_w ≈ 12.6. The small root also lies far outside the fitted range c ≥ 7 of the error models used to derive the formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the branch, e.g. take W_{-1} (equivalently require c_w > 1, or c_w inside the fitted range) in eq:cwW and in step 2 of Algorithm alg:parameter.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:parameter is not well defined as written; a literal implementation (e.g. MATLAB's lambertw, principal branch) returns a window parameter that cannot deliver the prescribed tolerance ε.
issues.title: Window parameter c_w is not determined by the stated Lambert W formula
issues.why_classification: A one-line branch specification makes the procedure well defined and restores the promised accuracy control, with no further mathematical content lost.

issues.failure_explanation: On the cell Q_k one only has |k| - √3/2 ≤ |x| ≤ |k| + √3/2, so monotonicity gives f(|x|) ≤ f(|k| - √3/2), not f(|k|) ≤ f(|x|); the cell-wise comparison used in the proof is invalid. The statement itself fails: with f = 1_{[0,1]} (nonincreasing and nonnegative) and K = 0.9 > √3/2, the left side equals 6 (the six lattice points of norm 1) while the right side is (4π/3)(1 - 0.034^3) ≈ 4.19.

failure_location.quote: Monotonicity of $f$ then yields the stated bound.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the bound to Σ_{|k|>K} f(|k|) ≤ ∫_{|x|>K-√3} f(|x|) dx, which follows at once from f(|k|) ≤ f(|x| - √3/2) on each unit cell and only shifts ω_* by √3π/L.
issues.overall_effect: The covering estimate used in the proof of Lemma lemma:dirsumerr_L2, and hence the radial reduction in Proposition prop:PSWF_split_errors, rests on a false lemma; the shift ω_* = ω_max - √3π/L is not justified as stated.
issues.title: Lattice covering lemma is false as stated
issues.why_classification: Changing the constant in the integration region is a short local repair that keeps every rate and guarantee; proving the constant as stated would instead require a nontrivial lattice-counting argument and is not the least repair.
